notes: Live Stripe FK-graph eval — the form-encoded / metadata-poor half of the cross-API anti-overfitting pair defined in docs/plans/agentprovider-cli-optimization-strategy.md (the AWX half is awx-fkgraph.json). Stripe is deliberately maximally different from AWX: form-encoded request bodies, no OPTIONS metadata (introspect runs in sample/reduced-confidence mode), gone_when tombstone reads (deleted customers read back 200 + deleted:true), last-item cursor pagination (cursor_from_item_field + starting_after), POST-as-update item paths, and a delete-less resource (price: destroy = forget/deactivate). A CLI or skill change validated only on AWX's DRF/OPTIONS shape is provisional until this eval also holds. Reference contracts for the same surface live in terraform-provider-dynamic/contracts/stripe_{product,price,customer}.yaml and stripe_customers.data.yaml — the agent under test must NOT read them (authoring from the skill alone is the point); they are the grader's oracle.
requires: Stripe test-mode credentials in stripe.env at the repo root (STRIPE_API_KEY, STRIPE_BASE_URL); test mode only — never a live-mode key
agentprovider CLI and terraform-provider-dynamic built from the current checkout

metric_schema.skill_version: git ref or skill snapshot under test
metric_schema.cli_version: agentprovider git ref or binary version under test
metric_schema.token_total: total agent tokens for the run
metric_schema.wall_seconds: elapsed seconds from first authoring command through verified cleanup
metric_schema.cmd_invocations: ordered list of every agentprovider invocation; the count is the primary efficiency metric
metric_schema.record_iterations: number of record attempts per contract
metric_schema.conform_iterations: number of conform attempts per contract
metric_schema.rerecord_count: number of forced rerecords after request-shape changes
metric_schema.source_reads: engine/provider/CLI source files read by the agent under test (hard floor 0)
metric_schema.manual_scaffold_edits: avoidable hand repairs to generated scaffold before the first successful record; do not count deterministic per-run conformance example values, fixture ids, or values learned from the first record
metric_schema.sensitivity_hand_edits: hand-added sensitive: true markings the scaffold should have seeded (target 0)
metric_schema.preamble_repetitions: raw env/export sequences repeated beyond the single setup.sh (target 0)
metric_schema.python_json_parses: inline python/jq spelunking of CLI JSON output where a --get/--path flag exists (target 0)
metric_schema.reference_loads: skill references/*.md files opened (low; 0 is ideal)
metric_schema.proof_quality: conform, completeness, mutation/proof, terraform, no-op-plan, and cleanup outcomes
metric_schema.cleanup_status: verified_clean, failed, or skipped with reason
metric_schema.generate_seconds: elapsed seconds for generate + the generated repo's replay test

setup: Run from the repository root; source stripe.env from its own directory without printing any value.
Stripe auth is a static bearer key — there is no per-run token mint/revoke step (that part of the AWX credential contract does not apply); the key must only ever appear as an env placeholder.
Export one RUN_TAG for the whole run; every created Stripe object carries apeval-${RUN_TAG}-fk-* in its name and a run_tag metadata key where the API allows metadata.
Pre-clean only stale apeval-* test-mode objects from earlier runs (deactivate stale prices, delete stale products/customers).

evals.name: stripe-fkgraph-full-pipeline
evals.prompt: Use the agentprovider skill to author a multi-resource Stripe (test mode) provider surface from a clean slate: three CRUD resources forming an FK graph — product, then price (FK: product id), then customer — plus a paginated customers data source (cursor pagination via the last item's id and starting_after). Follow the CLI-first loop end to end: introspect --expand (expect sample/reduced-confidence — Stripe has no OPTIONS metadata; say so in the report rather than fighting it), bootstrap --all --workflow-out, then one workflow run (preflight -> record -> prove -> generate), following the CLI 'next' hints rather than pre-scripting subcommands. Request bodies are form-encoded; deleted customers read back as 200 with deleted:true (model gone_when); prices cannot be deleted (model the delete-less destroy = forget path and deactivate in teardown). Then create one Terraform example with `agentprovider hcl` that wires the FK graph through computed ids (price.product references the product resource's id attribute), run a live terraform apply, verify a no-op second plan, and destroy. Finally run each generated repo's replay acceptance test (cd <out> && go mod tidy && go test ./internal/provider -run TestGeneratedReplay) — the eval is not done until replay passes. Use env placeholders for the key and base_url; never print credential values. Record every metric_schema field in a markdown table, including the ordered cmd_invocations list and every record/conform/prove attempt, forced rerecord, source read, and manual edit. Run teardown and fail the eval if any deletable apeval-${RUN_TAG}-fk-* object remains or any apeval-${RUN_TAG}-fk-* price remains active.

assertions.text: the final report includes every metric_schema field, with cmd_invocations as an ordered list
introspect is attempted before bootstrap and its sample/reduced-confidence result is reported as expected behavior for a metadata-poor API, not as an error
create/update request bodies are form-encoded via the contract's request_content_type, with no hand-written encoding workarounds and no manual cassette edits
the customer contract models the 200 + deleted:true tombstone via lifecycle.read.gone_when, proven by conformance and exercised by the destroy/recreate path
the price contract models the delete-less destroy (forget) path; teardown deactivates rather than pretends to delete
the customers data source uses last-item cursor pagination (cursor_from_item_field + starting_after) and returns multiple pages' items in conformance or live proof
the Terraform example wires price.product from the product resource's computed id (a real cross-resource reference, not a hardcoded id)
all four contracts pass agentprovider prove with 100% completeness and mutation_status passed_targeted before Terraform runtime proof
terraform apply succeeds for the FK-graph example, a second plan is a no-op, and destroy completes
each proven contract generates a standalone provider repo whose TestGeneratedReplay passes
teardown removes all deletable apeval-${RUN_TAG}-fk-* objects, deactivates all run-tagged prices, and verifies zero leftovers scoped to deletable types

efficiency_targets.note: Targets are comparison anchors, not proof. A run that reduces cost by skipping completeness, mutation proof, Terraform, pagination proof, or cleanup is a regression, not a win.

evals.cleanup: Terraform destroy first, then API sweep: deactivate every active apeval-${RUN_TAG}-fk-* price, delete every apeval-${RUN_TAG}-fk-* product and customer, verify list endpoints return zero active run-tagged objects for each deletable type (prices are delete-less — assert deactivated, not absent), and remove authored contracts, cassettes, proof sidecars, generated repos, and Terraform state from the workspace.
